string.text: Polytech
A former FICT student who has kept the strength of Polyana and the prudence of Dorm 8.
Faraday
A former KPI Telecom engineer who swapped his server room for a shack at the Forestry. Plans to start a business on anonymous data storage.
Rokovoy's router
A router from the FICT lab that Rokovoy brought back from China. Whatever is in its firmware, there are plenty of people in the Zone who want to get their hands on a router like this.
Find Faraday
Polytech asked you to find Faraday, who is holding on to Rokovoy's router. He is hiding in a hut at the Forestry.
Get the router from Faraday
Faraday has the router. Talk to him and get it.
Search Faraday's body
Faraday is dead. The router should still be on his body.
Escort Faraday to the Skadovsk
Faraday will give you the router if you get him to the Skadovsk. Bandits may attack on the way.
Return the router to Polytech
You have the router. Bring it to Polytech at the Skadovsk.
Got any work for me?
There's one thing. I want to get hold of a router.
What router?

When I studied at FICT, I took the course on networks and Linux. Rokovoy taught it back then, and during labs he would sometimes take out a modified router he had brought back from his internship in China. Strange casing, and firmware nobody ever really figured out. They say the most hardcore Chinese programmers wrote it, and the Chinese firewall runs on hardware like that.
How did it end up in the Zone?

When the department was getting rid of old equipment, the exhibit went off with the rest of the decommissioned hardware to the dealers who trade in that stuff. From there it travelled down the chain into the Zone. A rumour spread fast: there's a device that can be neither hacked nor tracked. After a rumour like that, the router's quiet life was over. Suddenly everyone with something to hide wanted it. Duty and Freedom first of all: each wants its own comms to stay private, and neither wants the other to get a thing like that. As soon as the router surfaced on the local markets, a real hunt began. It changed hands several times, but nobody managed to keep it for long. So bear in mind, you won't be the first one to go after it.
And why do you need it?

Half nostalgia, half principle. It's a piece of our department and a piece of my student years. I don't want it to become a trophy in Duty and Freedom's squabbles. And honestly, I'm curious what's in that firmware myself. What if the legends are true?
And who has it now?

Last I heard, it settled with a loner called Faraday. Not much is known about him. They say he used to work at KPI Telecom, and now he's building his own closed network in the Zone, a darknet of sorts. He wants to keep the secret data of the factions and ordinary stalkers alike: a neutral, unreachable keeper of other people's secrets. Rumour has it even the FAKS archive sits on his servers. He's holed up in a hut at the Forestry. He doesn't like strangers and takes everyone for either a faction agent or a bounty hunter.
What's the FAKS archive?

Ha, that's a legend of its own. The FAKS archive is one of the greatest mysteries of KPI. Nobody really knows what's in it: the senior students of those years just smile and change the subject. But I'm sending you for the router, not the archive.
Fine, I'll find your Faraday.
Deal, then. Bring me the router and I'll pay. And I wasn't joking about Duty and Freedom: watch your back.
I've got no time for this right now.
I understand.
I've brought Rokovoy's router.

Faraday gave it up himself? They must have really pressed him if he decided to quit. Pity, the idea of a neutral vault was a beautiful one. But there's no such thing as neutral in the Zone: sooner or later they come for you anyway.
So Faraday is gone... Not for me to judge you, the Zone is the Zone. But I'm sorry for the keeper of secrets: now all of them are gone with him.
And the FAKS archive?
The FAKS archive can stay a secret. Some secrets should stay unrevealed. Hand over the router, and here's what I promised. Thank you, stalker.
Stop right there! One more step and I shoot. Who are you? What do you want?
Polytech sent me. For Rokovoy's router.

Rokovoy's? I sat his networks exam too, passed on the third try... Alright, I believe you. Listen, since you're one of ours - I've got a deal for you. Bandits have been leaning on me. They want the router: someone told them Duty and Freedom would pay good money for it. They gave me time to think, they'll be back soon. I can't hold out here alone. Get me to the Skadovsk and the router's yours.
Deal. Let's go.
Quick, then, before they're back. You go first, I'll follow.
Easier to just take the router off you right now.
Right, another one. Go on then.
They say you've got the FAKS archive.
People say all sorts of things. Even if I do, it's none of your business.
That's it, we made it.
We did. They won't get me here. Won't last, though: if not these, others will come. As long as I've got the router, that's how it'll be. Forget it. I'm shutting down.
So, about the router?
A deal's a deal. Take it, bring it to your Polytech. And... thanks.
Max
A FICE student writing a diploma on electrical anomaly patterns. Came to the Zone for fieldwork. Lost his equipment in the Iron Forest and has been stuck on the Shevchenko ever since.
FPGA development board

An FPGA development board, rescued from a pile of written-off equipment in building 18. Thousands of logic cells, a dozen fast inputs and one desperate diploma depending on it. Keep away from Electras, rain and scientific advisors.
Burnt FPGA board

Used to be an FPGA development board. Now it's a piece of black textolite that smells like a soldering lab gone wrong. Technically it still has thousands of logic cells. None of them are logical anymore.
Cheap FPGA board

A cheap FPGA board from a Chinese marketplace. Delivery took three months, the manual is in a language nobody can identify. Too weak for Polytech's scanner, but perfect for a diploma: the committee won't notice.
The FPGA board was hit by a discharge. Burnt smell. That's not good.
Find Max
Polytech sent you to Max, a FICE student who lost his FPGA board in the Iron Forest. Look for him on the Shevchenko.
Retrieve the FPGA board from the Iron Forest
Max lost his FPGA board among the Electras in the Iron Forest. Find his backpack and take the board back.
Bring the board to Polytech
You have the FPGA board, intact or not. Take it to Polytech at the Skadovsk.
Take the cheap board to Max
Polytech handed over a cheap FPGA board instead. Take it to Max on the Shevchenko.
You look gloomy today. What's wrong?

My scanner. I'm building an artifact forecast scanner. I've got a pile of data from the anomaly fields: what appears where after an emission. The idea is simple: feed in the data, get a map of where to look. In practice my PDA just chokes on that stream.
And what do you need for it?

Hardware acceleration. An FPGA board: it processes signals in parallel, not one by one like the PDA. I've got one, a Chinese one. Too few logic cells, no fast inputs. Fine for a lab report, but for the Zone it's a toy.
Where do I get a proper one?

There's a kid on the "Shevchenko", Max. A FICE student, one of ours. He brought a serious development board to the Zone for his diploma. How he carried it here, I don't know and don't want to know. Go talk to him. Buy it, trade it, whatever. Just don't bully the kid.
All right, I'll talk to him.
Thanks. And if he starts talking about his diploma, just nod. It's faster.
Not now, I've got my own business.
Sure. The scanner isn't going anywhere. Unlike that kid's deadline.
About that FPGA board...
No board, no scanner. Max is on the "Shevchenko", if you haven't found him yet. And if you have, then you know more than I do.
I've brought the board.

Let me see... Not a single scratch. The architecture is intact, no breakdowns. You carried this through the Electras? That's precision work. I'll flash my configuration tonight, and the scanner will run like clockwork.
Here, you've earned every coin. And tell Max to stick to theory, he's no practitioner.
Oh, and one more thing. Take my Chinese board to him. It's useless to me, but for a diploma it's more than enough. Let the kid defend.
Damn it... Did you jump through an Electra with it? The textolite is black, the transistors are punched through. Did you skip physics at school?
There was a poltergeist throwing crates at me!

And there are Electras in the Iron Forest, I know. That's why it's called the Iron Forest and not the Botanical Garden. Fine. I'll sit down with a soldering iron and patch something together from what survived. Here's your pocket money, courier.
Still, take my Chinese board to Max. It's not his fault. For a diploma it's enough.
I'll take it to him.
About Max...
Have you taken him the board yet?
How's the scanner?
Humming like a server room. Max sent word, by the way: chapter three is ready. I didn't ask what that means.
Alive. Barely. It'll do.
Hi. How are you doing?
Twenty-nine days to my defence and no equipment. How do you think? Sorry. Not a good time.
Polytech says you have an FPGA board. Will you sell it?
I would, if I still had it. Sorry. Long story.
I'm in no hurry.

My diploma is about electrical anomalies. On paper the topic sounded great. So I came to the Zone for field data and went to the Iron Forest: there's a whole field of Electras at the old substation. I set everything up right inside, connected the probes... and then a crate flew past my head. Then another one. Nobody around, and everything is flying at me.
Where did a student even get a board like that?

Building 18. One of the labs was writing off old equipment, and there was a pile of it by the door. Nobody was ever going to look for it again. Old by university standards, but here it's the best thing for a hundred kilometres around.
A poltergeist.
I didn't stop to ask its name. I ran. My backpack got torn off on the way, and the board fell out. When I looked back, things were still flying around it.
So I just need to go there and pick it up?

It's not that simple. The board is lying there with no protection, right among the Electras. If you catch even one discharge while it's on you, the chips burn instantly. And that thing will throw everything it can find at you.
And your diploma?

My defence is in a month. A month! In the Zone. Where am I going to get a new board here, from a trader, between the vodka and the canned meat? My diploma is finished anyway. If you get the board out in one piece, take it to Polytech. At least someone will use it.
I'll get it.
Just... be careful. I don't want my diploma to have a casualty. The committee would definitely ask about it.
About your board...
It's in the Iron Forest, in the south-east of the substation, next to my backpack. And the poltergeist is there too, unless it's found a new hobby.
I've got your board.
You actually got it?! In one piece?! ...Right. Polytech. A deal's a deal. Take it to him before I change my mind.
Is that... it? It's black. Well. Maybe Polytech can still salvage something. Take it to him.
Polytech sent you this.
An FPGA? A real, working FPGA?! It's Chinese, but who cares! I've got a month, I can still make it! This time I'll redo the measurements somewhere without poltergeists.
And my old board... burnt, right? Fine. I'll put it in the "Limitations of the study" section.
Here, take this. It's an energy drink, my emergency supply. And if you ever need anything on the "Shevchenko", come to me.
Good luck with your defence.
If I pass, drinks are on me at the Polyana. If I live until Friday.
How's the diploma going?
Chapter three is ready. Chapter three is never ready. But it's ready.
Igorek
A legend of dorm No. 8. Lived there longer than anyone and ran the basement. They say he computed the sine of Monday.
Mad Armlet
Nobody really knows who he is or where he came from. Wears a black sweatshirt with white flames and shoots without warning.
Igorek's notes: napkin
A napkin from "Fora". Igorek drew a circle on it and wrote a few lines. You can examine it.
Igorek's notes: notebook page
A squared page torn out of a notebook. Igorek's handwriting. You can examine it.
Igorek's notes: last page
Another notebook page. Igorek's handwriting. You can examine it.
TOR-168
Igorek's AK-74 based rifle. Well kept and carefully zeroed: its owner clearly knows his weapons.\nMore accurate than a regular AK-74, has less recoil in bursts and wears out slower.
Igorek's notes
Polytech told the story of Igorek and the sine of Monday. According to Furka, Igorek's first page is hidden near the port cranes.
On the napkin Igorek wrote that the next page is "where they fuelled cars that have long been gone from here".
On the second page Igorek writes that the third page is at the burned farm. Mad Armlet holds out there.
Find Igorek

Igorek waits on the Skadovsk, at Beard's counter. He wrote the day and the hour on the last page as a sine and a cosine. He will ask what a week is, where Monday is on it, what its sine is and which day has the largest sine. The answers are in the notes.
Tell Polytech
Igorek accepted the exam. Polytech is waiting for the answer: how did Igorek compute the sine of Monday?
Why so thoughtful?
Max sent a note: he defended his thesis. Promises to buy everyone drinks on Friday. And as soon as I read it, I remembered dorm No. 8. Room two-oh-seven.
What is room two-oh-seven?

Two big guys lived there. On Fridays they threw parties and invited Crosshel, Cook, VladOS, General, Kvantur and Furka. Half of the guests did not even live in the dorm, they sneaked past the guard. I was there more often than in my own room. And I remember that room because of Igorek.
Who is Igorek?

A legend of the dorm. Lived there longer than anyone, ran the basement. One Friday we were sitting in two-oh-seven, had drunk a lot, and Igorek walked in. Cook was cooking at the time. Igorek sat down and said: "Guys, I computed the sine of Monday."
The sine... of Monday?

We asked the same. He explained it half the night: drew on a napkin, spun a bagel, talked about "Fora" and about Friday. I remember that it all added up. In the morning we only remembered bits and pieces, one thing here, another there, and nobody could put them together. By then Igorek had already left.
And what does the Zone have to do with it?

Furka came by the Skadovsk recently. He rarely comes to the Zone: stocks up on the famous cheese pancakes and disappears for half a year. So, he says Igorek is here too. And as always, Igorek explains nothing directly: he spread his notes over three stashes on Zaton, a page in each. According to Furka, the first one is near the port cranes.
You want me to collect them?

I want to know the answer. Collect the notes, figure it out and find Igorek. He pays well for right answers: whatever he gives you is yours. I only need to hear how he computed the sine of Monday. One more thing: I flashed the day of the week into your PDA. In the Zone all days are the same, but here you cannot do without it.
I have no time for sines right now.
Sines can wait. They are periodic, they will come back.
Any idea where to start with this sine?
A week ends, and then what? It starts again. What shape behaves like that?
And where does the sine come in?
A sine belongs to an angle. So Monday must have an angle. Remember where angles were measured from at school.
Where do I look for Igorek?

He wrote the place plainly and coded the time. Work out the day from the second page, all the angles are there. A day is a circle too: midnight is zero, an hour is fifteen degrees. But the cosine has two answers, at night and in the evening, so think when Igorek goes to a bar. And keep an eye on the day of the week in your PDA.
I found Igorek.
Seriously? So how did he compute the sine of Monday?
A week is a circle. Monday is on the right, at angle zero. The sine is the height of the point above the horizon, and for Monday it is zero.
He said it was a secret.
The sine of Monday is one. Monday is the first day, after all.
Zero. All these years, and it is zero. You know, this is the best zero of my life: it is not about "nothing", it is about where to count from.
I do not believe it. Igorek hides nothing, he just does not explain. Think again.
For Monday, it is the cosine that equals one. The sine is a height, not a number in a list. Think again.
Igorek asked me to tell you: back then you sat on Kvantur's bed and understood everything.
I did. And I understood. Then Cook brought cheese pancakes and it was all forgotten. Thank you, stalker. Here, this is from me. And tell everyone: Friday at nine on the Skadovsk. Drinks are on me.
I am here about the sine of Monday.
So you collected the notes and worked out the time. Then point by point: every right answer gets its share. First question: what is a week?
Let's go on. First question: what is a week?
Let's go on. Second question: where is Monday on the circle?
Let's go on. Third question: what is the sine of Monday?
Let's go on. Last question: which day has the largest sine?
A segment from Monday to Sunday.
A circle. After Sunday comes Monday again.
Five working days and two days off.
Right. Take these medkits, you will need them. Second question: where is Monday on the circle?
At the top, like twelve on a clock.
On the right, on the horizontal line, where the angle is zero.
At the bottom.
Right. Take the 5.45 rounds, you will soon see why. Third question: what is the sine of Monday?
One.
Zero.
Minus one.
Right: Monday lies on the horizontal line, its height is zero. Take this Kolobok. Last question: which day has the largest sine?
Friday.
Tuesday.
Wednesday.
Sunday.

Right: Wednesday is the closest to ninety degrees. Exam passed. Take my TOR-168: one hundred and sixty-eight hours in a week, not one extra. And I have to go. Tell Polytech: back then he sat on Kvantur's bed and understood everything. Let him remember.
No. Read the notes again and come next Friday. We will go on from this question.
No. For Monday, it is the cosine that equals one, and the sine is the height. Come next Friday, we will go on from this question.
By how it feels, yes. But on the circle Friday is below the horizontal line, its sine is negative. Come next Friday, we will go on from this question.
Shall we go on with the exam?
Not today. A week is a circle, Friday will come back.
Will we meet again?
Sure. On Friday. A week is a circle.
